title: The Region 6 Wrap: Brazil's 71% Pay Gap, Jamaica's Rate Rise, Guyana Oil | Across the Water, Ep. 19
lede: The week of Nov 16 in the business of the African diaspora: IBGE finds white workers in Brazil earned 71% more than Black workers in 2025, the real hits its weakest close since April 2025, the Bank of Jamaica raises its rate to 6.50%, Guyana's oil capacity reaches 1.1 million barrels a day, and the Executive Leadership Council names Lisa Osborne Ross CEO. Plus Caribbean currencies and the latest Black unemployment rate.
keyPoints: White workers in Brazil earned R$4,425 a month on average in 2025, 71% more than Black workers (R$2,585); Black and pardo Brazilians are 55.1% of workers but 30.7% of managers (IBGE, Nov 18).
The dollar closed at R$5.93 on Nov 19, the real's weakest close since April 2025; Brazil's Senate passed the fiscal adjustment bill 69–2 on Nov 18 (Agência Brasil, Diario de Pernambuco).
The Bank of Jamaica raised its policy rate 50 bps to 6.50% from Nov 19; October inflation was 8.2% (Bank of Jamaica).
ExxonMobil started Uaru on Nov 16, lifting Guyana's installed capacity to 1.1 million barrels a day (ExxonMobil).
The Executive Leadership Council named Lisa Osborne Ross president and CEO from Jan 15, 2027 (ELC via PR Newswire).
